title: Polynomial-time zero-error verifier characterization
statement: Let $L$ be a language of bit strings. If $L$ belongs to the class defined as the union, over natural numbers $c$, of languages decidable by a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with expected running-time bound $n^c+1$ in the stated polynomial-time model, then $L$ has an efficient polynomial-witness verifier that never gives an incorrect answer and gives no answer with probability at most $1/2$.
hypotheses_covered: $L$ is a language of bit strings
$L$ belongs to the union over natural $c$ of the stated expected-time zero-error classes
